sentences.gloss: The bread at the market is cheap.
The buses in the city are slow.
I don’t have a new car.
The old house is far away.
The old man is in the park.
Is there a good restaurant here?
The little children are at home.
I (m.) want a glass of cold water.
The new book is on the table.
The new books are on the table.
The old bed is in the room.
The young women are in the park.
The small glasses are in the cupboard.
The brown table is in the living room.
I (m.) want a light blue bag.

sentences.text: אַתָּה רוֹצֶה יַיִן לָבָן אוֹ אָדֹם?
sentences.gloss: Do you (m.) want white or red wine?
The yellow lamp is on the table.
The blue glasses are in the kitchen.
The house is bigger than the flat.
The houses are bigger than the flats.
The train is faster than the bus.
Is the train faster than the bus?
The son is taller than Dad.
The daughter is taller than Dad.
The city is more beautiful than the village.
Is the city more beautiful than the village?
I (m.) am more tired than yesterday.
I (f.) am more tired than yesterday.
Today it is hotter than yesterday.
He is the youngest in the family.
Grandma is the oldest in the family.
I have more books than the teacher.
The black bag is cheaper than the red one.
The kitchen is brighter than the living room.

sentences.text: מָה יוֹתֵר טוֹב, תֵּה אוֹ קָפֶה?
sentences.gloss: What is better, tea or coffee?
alts: מָה טוֹב יוֹתֵר, תֵּה אוֹ קָפֶה?

sentences.gloss: The house is small, but it is beautiful.
The houses are small, but they are beautiful.
I (m.) am hungry, but there is no bread.
The house is beautiful but expensive.

sentences.text: הוּא אוֹהֵב קָפֶה, אֲבָל הִיא אוֹהֶבֶת תֵּה.
sentences.gloss: He likes coffee, but she likes tea.

sentences.text: אֲנִי שׁוֹתֶה מַיִם כִּי אֲנִי צָמֵא.
sentences.gloss: I (m.) drink water because I am thirsty.

sentences.text: אֲנִי שׁוֹתָה מַיִם כִּי אֲנִי צְמֵאָה.
sentences.gloss: I (f.) drink water because I am thirsty.

sentences.text: הוּא לֹא בָּא כִּי הוּא עָיֵף.
sentences.gloss: He isn’t coming because he is tired.

sentences.text: לָמָּה אַתָּה לֹא אוֹכֵל? כִּי אֲנִי לֹא רָעֵב.
sentences.gloss: Why aren’t you (m.) eating? Because I’m not hungry.

sentences.text: אֲנִי לֹא הוֹלֵךְ לַפַּארְק כִּי קַר.
sentences.gloss: I (m.) am not going to the park because it is cold.

sentences.text: אֲנִי עָיֵף, לָכֵן אֲנִי נִשְׁאָר בַּבַּיִת.
sentences.gloss: I (m.) am tired, so I am staying at home.

sentences.text: אֲנִי עֲיֵפָה, לָכֵן אֲנִי נִשְׁאֶרֶת בַּבַּיִת.
sentences.gloss: I (f.) am tired, so I am staying at home.

sentences.text: הַמּוֹנִית יְקָרָה, לָכֵן אֲנַחְנוּ נוֹסְעִים בְּאוֹטוֹבּוּס.
sentences.gloss: The taxi is expensive, so we go by bus.
I (m.) am hungry, so I am eating.
I (f.) am hungry, so I am eating.
It is cold outside, so the children are at home.

sentences.text: אֲנִי אוֹכֵל אֲרוּחַת בֹּקֶר, וְאָז אֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ לָעֲבוֹדָה.
sentences.gloss: I (m.) eat breakfast, and then I go to work.

sentences.text: הוּא קוֹנֶה לֶחֶם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוּא חוֹזֵר הַבַּיְתָה.
sentences.gloss: He buys bread, and then he goes back home.
When I (m.) am tired, I drink coffee.
When I (f.) am tired, I drink coffee.

sentences.text: כְּשֶׁהוּא רָעֵב, הוּא אוֹכֵל לֶחֶם עִם גְּבִינָה.
sentences.gloss: When he is hungry, he eats bread with cheese.
When it is hot outside, we go to the park.
I (m.) go home when I am tired.
When the teacher comes, the students are happy.

sentences.text: אִם אַתָּה צָמֵא, יֵשׁ מַיִם בַּמְּקָרֵר.
sentences.gloss: If you (m.) are thirsty, there is water in the fridge.

sentences.text: אִם אַתְּ צְמֵאָה, יֵשׁ מַיִם בַּמְּקָרֵר.
sentences.gloss: If you (f.) are thirsty, there is water in the fridge.
If you (m.) are cold, don’t go out.
If you (f.) are cold, don’t go out.

sentences.text: אִם הַמּוֹנִית יְקָרָה, אֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ בָּרֶגֶל.
sentences.gloss: If the taxi is expensive, I (m.) walk.

sentences.text: אִם אַתָּה רוֹצֶה, אֲנִי מְבַשֵּׁל מָרָק.
sentences.gloss: If you (m.) want, I’ll cook soup.

sentences.text: אִם אֵין לֶחֶם, אֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ לַסּוּפֶּר.
sentences.gloss: If there is no bread, I (m.) go to the supermarket.
If you (m.) come tomorrow, I am at home.
I (m.) am glad that you (m.) are here.
I (f.) am glad that you (m.) are here.
It’s good that you (f.) are at home.
Of course he is coming (it is clear that he is coming).

sentences.text: הוּא הוֹלֵךְ לָעֲבוֹדָה לַמְרוֹת שֶׁהוּא עָיֵף.
sentences.gloss: He goes to work although he is tired.

sentences.text: הִיא הוֹלֶכֶת לָעֲבוֹדָה לַמְרוֹת שֶׁהִיא עֲיֵפָה.
sentences.gloss: She goes to work although she is tired.
Although the house is old, it is beautiful.

sentences.text: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא רָעֵב, הוּא לֹא אוֹכֵל.
sentences.gloss: Although he is hungry, he doesn’t eat.
alts: לַמְרוֹת שֶׁהוּא רָעֵב, הוּא לֹא אוֹכֵל.
